thread:
incbot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: privconnect-eu-west1 ECMP path oscillation. 5 customer circuits reporting intermittent 504s/connection resets to their private endpoints. Severity: P2. auto-attach runbook: privconnect/ecmp-flap.

morgan: Seeing alerts for BGP flaps on multiple peer-sets in eu-west1b/ew1c. Metrics spike in packet loss + TCP retransmits around 09:22 UTC.

jessica: Confirmed. BFD sessions between our edge and CloudProv fabric are dropping then re-establishing every ~30s. Route churn visible for 10.20.0.0/24 (AcmeCorp) and a couple more customer prefixes. ECMP seems to be oscillating between two equal-cost paths.

sam: tagging netops and oncall: @jessica can you attach the quick traceroutes + relevant bgp show output? I want to see asymmetry.

jessica: Paste below — traceroute from gw-eu-west1b to Acme private IP
```
traceroute to 10.20.0.55 (10.20.0.55), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1  0.42 ms  0.41 ms  0.39 ms
 2  203.0.113.2  1.2 ms  1.3 ms  1.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.7  12.3 ms  *  12.1 ms
 4  198.51.100.9  24.5 ms  24.6 ms  24.4 ms
 5  10.20.0.55  25.8 ms  26.0 ms  25.7 ms
```
and current BGP summary snippet:
```
Neighbor        AS      MsgRcvd  MsgSent  State/PfxRcd
203.0.113.2     64512   12456    12458    12
198.51.100.7    64513   12399    12401    10
```

acme-eng: We're getting frequent 504s in our app stack, started ~09:20 UTC. Users can't reach internal webhooks — this is impacting critical sync jobs. Currently degraded for ~40% of requests.

morgan: marking customer impact. Routing shows both neighbors advertising the same prefixes with identical local-pref/med; ECMP chosen but BFD instability causes one path to drop briefly, traffic flips, then packet reordering/outs-of-order causing app timeouts.

leo: Oncall handoff in 10 minutes. I'll take lead during the blast window. @jessica coordinate with CloudProv support (ticket CP-789123) and set temporary mitigation.

jessica: Proposed mitigations (fast):
- Temporarily withdraw the less-stable path (neighbor 198.51.100.7) from our edge to stop oscillation
- If withdraw not possible, set community to prefer 203.0.113.2 via local-preference bump
- Short-term: enable TCP reordering buffer on egress for affected prefixes (if safe)

sam: Also consider adding a per-customer prefix pinned route on our routing fabric to avoid ECMP for these prefixes until we stabilize.

morgan: Performing the withdraw on a test peer first. Commands:
```
# advertise-route with prepended AS to influence CloudProv
bgp advertise 10.20.0.0/24 next-hop 100.64.0.2 prepend-as 64500
# or on our side withdraw the neighbor session (controlled)
configure terminal
neighbor 198.51.100.7 shutdown
```
I will do withdraw for 198.51.100.7 in eu-west1c at 09:35 UTC and observe.

jessica: Confirmed with CloudProv — they see BFD flaps correlated to a microburstable CPU event on fabric-switch-8 in ew1c. They will attempt a graceful powercycle of that switch; meanwhile they advised us to steer traffic to ew1b.

acme-eng: Please keep us updated. If you withdraw a path, do you expect full recovery or transient effects for a few minutes?

leo: Expect transient reconvergence for ~30-90s. We'll post exact windows. I'll DM AcmeCorp with ETA and post an incident update to status.redwood.ai.

morgan: Done — withdrew neighbor 198.51.100.7 from the edge in eu-west1c at 09:35 UTC. Monitoring now. Route table shows single active path to 10.20.0.0/24 via 203.0.113.2.

jessica: CloudProv confirms move to ew1b-only and reports switch reboot started at 09:36 UTC.

(5m later)

morgan: Metrics improving: TCP retransmits down 80%, app timeouts down to ~5% of prior. No additional BFD flaps observed.

acme-eng: We're seeing recovery on our side — queued jobs are catching up. Thanks. Any action post-reboot?

jessica: After CloudProv completes hardware remediation, we'll reintroduce the second path under a controlled maintenance window and put stricter BFD timers + hold-down to avoid immediate reintroduce. Proposed plan:
- Wait for stable BFD for 30m
- Re-add path with conservative timers: bfd min_rx 1000 min_tx 1000 detect_mult 3
- Monitor for 1h, then return to normal timers if stable

sam: Logging runbook actions into incident ticket IN-4589 and adding a post-incident action item for automated path-preference rules for customers with private connect dependencies.

leo: I'll make a public incident message now: short summary + customer impact + mitigation + ETA for re-add. Also scheduling postmortem with NetOps and CloudProv tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

incbot: Incident documented: IN-4589. Status: mitigated (partial). Notifications: sent to affected customers and pubstatus updated.

morgan: Closing active pager. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes and timeline updates. If anyone sees new flaps, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
